data.cultural_impact: The name Shivangi carries the blessings and grace of God Shiva, the Hindu deity revered for his omnipotence, destruction of evil, and transformation. The name is a popular choice among Hindus and is often given to girls as a sign of auspicious blessings and divine protection.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shivangi signifies the divine grace and blessings bestowed upon an individual by the supreme deity Lord Shiva. It is a reminder of the protective and transformative power of the deity and the importance of seeking his blessings for spiritual growth and inner peace.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Shivangi was an avatar or incarnation of Goddess Parvati. She is also known as 'Sati-Savitri' or 'Mother of All', and is believed to have manifested herself during the Satya Yuga (Golden Age). She is said to have protected and nurtured the universe until it was destroyed and a new one was created.

Another reference to Shivangi comes from the epic Mahabharata. In this context, she is mentioned as the wife of King Janamejaya, the grandson of Arjuna. She is also known as the goddess Hingula, and is believed to have been the mother of two important characters in the epic – Bhishma and Vidura.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shivangi has roots in Indian mythology, referencing the Hindu god Shiva. It is now popularly used as a modern name for girls in various contexts, including spiritual and artistic expressions. On Instagram, some accounts dedicated to Hinduism and spirituality showcase images of the god Shiva and incorporating the name Shivangi in their descriptions. On TikTok, trends of Hindu-inspired dance challenges and storytelling using the name Shivangi have emerged. On Pinterest, boards featuring Hindu deities, Hindu-inspired home decor, and spiritual art display the name Shivangi as a symbol of spirituality and connection to Indian heritage.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Lakshmi Shivangi in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Shivangi, which means "Goddess Shiva's Grace". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
